newsitem.title: UK: Phase 2 of U.K. gas competition to start Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: Phase 2 of U.K. gas competition to start Jan 13.

text.p: Britain's gas regulator Ofgas has proposed introducing domestic gas competition for a second pilot area of 1.5 million households in southwest and southeast England in two stages, starting next January.

Ofgas Director General Clare Spottiswoode proposed in a consultation document published on Wednesday that domestic customers in Dorset and the former county of Avon should be able to choose their gas suppliers from January 13, 1997.
And competition should open to domestic consumers in Kent, East and West Sussex from February 7.
"Already fifteen percent of customers have transferred from British Gas to competitors who are offering lower prices.
"It is important that we move to the next phase as early as possible to give more people the option of cheaper gas," Spottiswoode said.

A spokesman for Ofgas said the reason for introducing the second pilot area in two stages was concern over the numbers involved. "We want a smooth transition without a spike of people wanting to change on day one", he said.

The first pilot area, covering 500,000 consumers in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, opened for competition on April 29, and Ofgas says 70,000 conmsumers have switched away from British Gas to a new supplier.
But the second pilot area covers three times this number, leading Ofgas to try and stagger the introduction of phase two to avoid system problems.
Phase three, covering 19 million consumers throughout England, Scotland and Wales will be introduced during 1998 although no date has not been set.
Ofgas invites comments on its proposal document, "Extension of domestic competition," by October 9.
